note: The owner's starter task list, shipped so a new journey begins with a full journal. Importing a task file replaces it.

tasks.title: Wake Up at 5
tasks.notes: Start the day on purpose. If the exact time shifts, the win is waking at the planned time instead of drifting.

tasks.title: Make My Bed
tasks.notes: Quick environmental win. Signal that the day has started and the room is not left in chaos.

tasks.title: Brush My Teeth - Morning
tasks.notes: Basic hygiene anchor. Keep it boring and automatic.

tasks.title: Feed Finn & Refill Water
tasks.notes: Feed Finn and make sure his water is full.

tasks.title: Take supplements
tasks.notes: Take prescribed meds and regular supplements consistently.

tasks.title: Sunlight in the Morning
tasks.notes: Get outside or near bright natural light early to help energy, mood, and circadian rhythm.

tasks.title: Outside Before Screens
tasks.notes: When possible, get outside before recreational screens: sunlight, walk, prayer, yard, or trail. Real world before digital worlds.

tasks.title: Meditation / Stillness
tasks.notes: 5-10 minutes of silence, breathing, prayerful stillness, or mindfulness. The goal is calm control, not perfection.

tasks.title: Read the Bible
tasks.notes: Read Scripture with attention. Small faithful reading counts more than perfect volume.

tasks.title: Morning Oath / Pray Alone
tasks.notes: Pray by yourself honestly. Bring gratitude, stress, repentance, needs, and obedience before God. Speak your values with conviction: husband, father, Christian, leader, disciplined man.

tasks.title: Help in the Morning
tasks.notes: Look for one practical way to help the household morning go smoother: girls, dishes, bags, clothes, cleanup, or Megan support.

tasks.title: Train the Body
tasks.notes: Lift, walk, cardio, boxing, hike, or another meaningful movement session. On rest days, an intentional walk counts.

tasks.title: Mobility Workout
tasks.notes: Mobility routine, stretching, soft tissue, decompression, or recovery work. Keep your body usable, not just strong.

tasks.title: Daily work review
tasks.notes: Check team queues, stuck work, volume, and tickets at risk of breaching. Surface what needs action in standup or with the right person.

tasks.title: Project Work
tasks.notes: Protected time on high-value work: Knowledge Ecosystem, ServiceNow, KCS, dashboards, process improvement, strategy, or leadership systems.

tasks.title: Clear Emails
tasks.notes: Clear or triage work/personal email. Aim for control, not perfection.

tasks.title: Clear Texts & Messages
tasks.notes: Clear or triage texts, Teams/Slack, and other important messages that need a response.

tasks.title: Phone Boundaries Kept
tasks.notes: Avoid default scrolling, especially during family time, bedtime, and work focus blocks.

tasks.title: Name It Before I React
tasks.notes: When triggered, anxious, angry, or impatient, pause and name the emotion: 'I'm feeling ___ because ___.' Then choose the next faithful action.

tasks.title: Healthy Food Default
tasks.notes: Prioritize protein, vegetables, reasonable calories, hydration, and mostly healthy foods without letting cravings drive the day. If edibles are used, avoid uncontrolled pantry/freezer spirals and stick to a pre-decided snack or meal.

tasks.title: Guard the Gate
tasks.notes: No porn, no edging, no searching, no testing the boundary, and no 'almost porn.' Also avoid upstream triggers like lust-scrolls, thirst traps, and fantasy rabbit holes. If tempted, do one interrupt action: pray, walk, shower, leave the room, message accountability, or go to bed.

tasks.title: Protein Anchor
tasks.notes: Hit protein target or include a clear protein source at each main meal. Protein first, cravings second.

tasks.title: Vegetables With Meals
tasks.notes: Include vegetables with lunch and dinner, or every main meal when realistic. Greens supplements can support but not replace this habit.

tasks.title: Walk the Realm
tasks.notes: Hit step goal or take an intentional walk. On low-energy days, a purposeful walk still counts as movement leadership.

tasks.title: Boxing / Conditioning Rep
tasks.notes: Short boxing, bag work, conditioning, intervals, or skill work. Keep it sustainable; it can be a bonus movement rep rather than mandatory hard training.

tasks.title: Capture Beauty
tasks.notes: Take one intentional iPhone photo of something meaningful, beautiful, funny, or family-related. Collect moments instead of loot.

tasks.title: Spend With Wisdom
tasks.notes: No impulse purchases. Use the 24-hour cart rule for non-urgent items and make spending intentional rather than frictionless.

tasks.title: End-of-Day Work Shutdown
tasks.notes: Clear the work to-do list, identify tomorrow's top priorities, close loops, and mentally leave work.

tasks.title: No Phone Around Girls
tasks.notes: When you are with Emmy and Liv, be with them. Phone away unless truly needed. This can also count during wider family time when presence matters.

tasks.title: Ten-Minute Miracle - Emmy
tasks.notes: At least 10 minutes of focused connection with Emmy. Let her lead when possible. No multitasking.

tasks.title: Ten-Minute Miracle - Liv
tasks.notes: At least 10 minutes of focused connection with Liv. Let her lead when possible. No multitasking.

tasks.title: Emmy Homework / School Growth
tasks.notes: Homework, reading, school prep, encouragement, or helping Emmy build confidence around school responsibilities.

tasks.title: Pray Before Dinner
tasks.notes: Simple family prayer before dinner. Builds household culture, not just personal faith.

tasks.title: Repair Quickly
tasks.notes: If you were impatient, distracted, harsh, or disconnected, apologize and reconnect. This is a character habit.

tasks.title: One Load of Laundry
tasks.notes: Start, switch, fold, or put away one load. Any meaningful laundry step counts if it moves the household forward.

tasks.title: Pick Up Dog Poops
tasks.notes: Keep the yard under control. A daily check counts; pick up when needed. Small unpleasant task that prevents bigger unpleasantness later.

tasks.title: 10 Minutes Cleaning
tasks.notes: Clean or reset one area for 10 minutes: kitchen, toys, counters, living room, bedroom, garage, or clutter zone.

tasks.title: Household Contribution
tasks.notes: Do one practical home task that actually helps today beyond the automatic basics: dishes, trash, restocking, logistics, cleanup, or support.  Also notice repairs, purchases, scheduling, organizing, and unfinished household loops without waiting to be asked.

tasks.title: Daily Affection & Pursuit
tasks.notes: Show Megan warm physical affection and, when appropriate, pursue her playfully or romantically. Keep marriage from becoming only logistics.

tasks.title: Turn Toward One Bid
tasks.notes: Notice and respond warmly to at least one connection bid from Megan: comment, question, joke, complaint, touch, request, or invitation.

tasks.title: Connection Questions
tasks.notes: Ask Megan something real. Listen without fixing unless she wants solutions. The goal is emotional connection.

tasks.title: Say Thank You
tasks.notes: Thank Megan specifically for something she did, carried, handled, or endured. Can also apply to the girls or others when appropriate.

tasks.title: Serve Megan Unasked
tasks.notes: Do one thing that lightens her load without needing credit: dishes, girls, cleanup, logistics, bedtime help, or emotional support.

tasks.title: Read / Learn Something Useful
tasks.notes: Read, listen, or learn for 20 minutes. The win is not just consuming content but taking away one useful insight for faith, marriage, parenting, fitness, work, or life.

tasks.title: Stop When Bored
tasks.notes: If gaming becomes boredom, obligation, checklist clearing, or 'one more thing,' stop. Boredom is the cue to exit, not grind harder.

tasks.title: Evening Shutdown / Tomorrow Prep
tasks.notes: Close loops, prep for tomorrow, reduce phone stimulation, check calendar, and make the next morning easier.

tasks.title: Daily Values Review
tasks.notes: Ask: Did I live like the man I say I want to be? Note one win and one adjustment. Best done later in the day if morning feels too early.

tasks.title: Lights-Out Consistency
tasks.notes: Get in bed on time and protect the sleep window. This is tracked separately because sleep is foundational.

tasks.title: Clear Physical Mail & Paper Clutter
tasks.notes: Open, toss, file, or act on physical mail and small paper clutter so it does not become background stress.

tasks.title: Note for Megan
tasks.notes: Write her a note, text, card, or voice memo that encourages her specifically.

tasks.title: Practice Photography / iPhone Mastery
tasks.notes: Take, edit, organize, or intentionally practice photography. Prioritize low-friction iPhone mastery unless you intentionally choose to practice with the camera.

tasks.title: Family Adventure / Intentional Outing
tasks.notes: Do something intentional with the family: park, walk, hike, library, breakfast, church event, movie night, backyard game, board/card game, or outdoor outing.

tasks.title: Game-Free / Sabbath Rhythm
tasks.notes: One intentional block or day where gaming does not lead. Prioritize worship, family, rest, reading, outside time, recovery, or Oathforge execution over app/game refinement.

tasks.title: Weekly Life Review
tasks.notes: Review habits, habit cards/tasks, calendar, misses, wins, family needs, work priorities, and what needs to change next week. Look for friction, not just failure.

tasks.title: Marriage Date / Connection Block
tasks.notes: Plan intentional time with Megan: date night, at-home date, walk, coffee, shared activity, or deeper conversation.

tasks.title: Fair Play / Household Ownership Check
tasks.notes: Ask: What am I fully owning from conception to planning to execution, not just helping with?

tasks.title: Family Memory Capture
tasks.notes: Save photos, print pictures, write down funny kid moments, update an album, preserve family memories, or use iPhone photography to capture real life with the girls.  Also save funny quotes, milestone videos, school art, traditions, and print or organize favorite memories.

tasks.title: Friendship / Hospitality Touchpoint
tasks.notes: Invite someone over, plan a hangout, schedule a call, or invest in another couple/family/friendship.

tasks.title: Home Declutter Zone
tasks.notes: Pick one zone: drawer, closet, toys, garage shelf, office, clothes, pantry, bathroom, etc. Finish one contained area.

tasks.title: Family Protection Review
tasks.notes: Review insurance coverage, beneficiaries, emergency information, estate documents, important account access, and unresolved family administrative needs. Turn any gaps into concrete next actions.  Also review passwords, shared documents, utilities, taxes, registrations, renewals, beneficiaries, and emergency information.

tasks.title: Reset Ritual
tasks.notes: The bridge out of the window: stand up, water, two-minute walk, review the next task. This transition prevents the second session better than any rule.

tasks.title: Monthly Review
tasks.notes: One sit-down, three lenses: (1) Identity - who am I becoming, are the four roles being lived? (2) Oathforge Audit - is the app serving the habits or replacing them? (3) 30-Day Household Reset - what needs a reset next month?

tasks.title: Log Meals & Weigh In
tasks.notes: Built With Science ritual: morning weigh-in + log every meal. You did this religiously once - the data kept you honest. Weigh first thing; log as you eat, not from memory at night.

tasks.title: Steward’s Weekly Review
tasks.notes: Walk the 25 areas at the week’s start — Notice · Plan · Execute · Close the Loop. Plans forge quests automatically.

tasks.title: One Intentional Touchpoint
tasks.notes: Ping one direct report about THEIR thing - not a status ask, just presence. Rotate through the team so Friday's gut check is already answered.

tasks.title: Recognize One Person (Specific Praise)
tasks.notes: One specific, named praise - Slack counts. Name the exact action and its impact. Specific beats grand.

tasks.title: Clear One Blocker
tasks.notes: Remove one obstacle for someone on the team today - an approval, an escalation, a decision they're waiting on.

tasks.title: Ask Before Answering
tasks.notes: Ask one good question before giving one answer. Coach the thinking, don't just dispense the fix.
